# The live browser's one extra path out of a tenant namespace: TCP 8080 to the
# relay, from a live-browser pod, and nothing else
# (docs/design/live-browser.md §3.3 and §8.3; lane LB-L6, part of #1030).
#
# A `claude-code-browser` pod's live gate DIALS OUT to `swarm-live` -- the
# single-replica relay StatefulSet in `swarm-system` -- over plain ws on 8080. The
# pod listens on nothing; `default-deny.yaml` still denies all ingress here,
# and nothing in this file touches that.
#
# WHY A SECOND POLICY AND NOT A FIFTH RULE IN `allow-egress.yaml`. That
# policy's internet rule is an `ipBlock`, and on Dataplane V2 "Pod traffic is
# never covered by an ipBlock rule" (its header records the measurement), so
# no edit to rule 4 can reach the relay pod. A pod-to-pod path needs a pod
# selector, and it must name ONE destination: the relay pods in ONE namespace,
# never "every pod in swarm-system". NetworkPolicies are unions, so this adds
# exactly that path and removes nothing; the existing policy renders
# byte-identical (tests/unit/scripts/test_live_netpol.py holds its digest).
#
# WHY A LABEL, NOT `podSelector: {}`. `allow-egress.yaml` selects every pod for
# a reason its comment gives (a label the dispatcher did not set would leave a
# browser task with no DNS). That reason does not apply here: a pod missing
# `swarm-live: enabled` simply has no live path, and its DNS and internet
# still come from the existing policy. The label is set by the dispatcher,
# never by a caller -- `scheduler.dispatch.LIVE_POD_LABEL`, on live-browser
# pods only -- so only a pod whose profile is `live_browser` in the frozen
# catalogue can reach the relay (invariant 10). Every other agent in this
# namespace, and anything one of them spawns, cannot open the socket at all.
#
# WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO. It does not make the relay trust the pod. The relay
# admits a tunnel only with a one-use ticket swarm-api minted for this
# session, tenant, attempt and generation (§3.3, §5.2); this policy only
# decides who may knock. The agent shares the worker's network namespace
# (`allow-egress.yaml`, WHAT RULE 2 COSTS), so the agent child can open the
# same socket -- and holds no ticket for it, because the ticket travels over
# ctl.sock and is never in an environment variable, a file or `work/`.
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: swarm-allow-live-egress
  namespace: swarm-tenant-u-alice
  labels:
    managed-by: swarm-terraform
    swarm-tenant: u-alice
spec:
  # Must equal scheduler.dispatch.LIVE_POD_LABEL; test_live_netpol.py holds
  # the two together.
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      swarm-live: "enabled"
  policyTypes:
    - Egress
  egress:
    # ONE peer with BOTH selectors: the relay pods in swarm-system. Two list
    # items -- a namespaceSelector and a podSelector -- would be an OR, and
    # would open every pod in swarm-system, or every relay-named pod in this
    # namespace.
    - to:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: swarm-system
          podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app.kubernetes.io/name: swarm-live
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 8080
---
# The proxied browser's one extra path out of a tenant namespace: TCP 3128 to
# swarm-egress, from a pod the dispatcher labelled for proxied egress, and
# nothing else (docs/browser-egress.md §2.5; lane EGRESS-SVC, part of #1030).
#
# Built exactly like `swarm-allow-live-egress` (allow-live-egress.yaml), for
# the same reason: the internet rule in `allow-egress.yaml` is an ipBlock, and
# "Pod traffic is never covered by an ipBlock rule", so reaching a pod in
# swarm-system needs a pod selector naming ONE destination.
#
# WHY A LABEL. `swarm-egress: proxy` is set by the dispatcher on a live-browser
# pod whose tenant and profile are switched on (lane EGRESS-DISPATCH), never
# by a caller (invariant 10). A pod without it simply has no proxy path; its
# DNS and direct internet still come from the existing policy. NetworkPolicies
# are unions, so this adds exactly that path and removes nothing.
#
# WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO. It does not make swarm-egress trust the pod.
# swarm-egress serves a CONNECT only with an attempt ticket swarm-api minted
# for this tenant, task, attempt and generation; this policy only decides who
# may knock. The agent shares the pod's network namespace, so it can open the
# socket too -- and holds no ticket, which reaches the gate over ctl.sock and
# is never in an environment variable, a file or `work/`.
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: swarm-allow-egress-proxy
  namespace: swarm-tenant-u-alice
  labels:
    managed-by: swarm-terraform
    swarm-tenant: u-alice
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      swarm-egress: "proxy"
  policyTypes:
    - Egress
  egress:
    # ONE peer with BOTH selectors: the swarm-egress pods in swarm-system.
    - to:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: swarm-system
          podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app.kubernetes.io/name: swarm-egress
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 3128
---
# The internal judge's one extra path out of a tenant namespace: TCP 8443 to
# the decision-api forwarder in swarm-system -- the only route onto Saga's
# Tailscale tailnet -- from a pod the dispatcher labelled
# `swarm-judge: internal`, and nothing else (owner decisions 2026-10-14; lane
# JUDGE-NET; kubernetes/swarm-system/tailscale-egress.yaml,
# docs/runbooks/tailscale-egress.md).
#
# Built exactly like `swarm-allow-live-egress` and `swarm-allow-egress-proxy`,
# for the same reason: the internet rule in `allow-egress.yaml` is an ipBlock,
# and "Pod traffic is never covered by an ipBlock rule", so reaching a pod in
# swarm-system needs a pod selector naming ONE destination. 8443 is the
# forwarder's port; callers dial the Service's 443, and Dataplane V2 judges
# the connection after the Service's DNAT, at the pod and its 8443.
#
# WHY A LABEL. `swarm-judge: internal` is set by the dispatcher on a
# live-browser or agent pod whose Jev judgment backend is an internal one
# ("Internal Jev", the default, or "Internal Laya"), never by a caller
# (invariant 10). A pod without it -- a TypeSafe-backed one included -- has no
# route to the tailnet at all; its DNS and direct internet still come from the
# existing policy. NetworkPolicies are unions, so this adds exactly that path
# and removes nothing.
#
# WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO. It does not choose where on the tailnet the pod goes:
# the forwarder dials one host on one port, and the tailnet's own ACL grants
# its node nothing else.
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: swarm-allow-judge-egress
  namespace: swarm-tenant-u-alice
  labels:
    managed-by: swarm-terraform
    swarm-tenant: u-alice
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      swarm-judge: "internal"
  policyTypes:
    - Egress
  egress:
    # ONE peer with BOTH selectors: the forwarder pods in swarm-system.
    - to:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: swarm-system
          podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app.kubernetes.io/name: decision-api-egress
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 8443
---
# The shared graph service's path out of a tenant namespace: TCP 8080 to the
# swarm-graph pods in swarm-system, from any pod in the namespace, and nothing
# else (docs/design/graph-service.md §2.1; lane GS-INFRA, part of #1384;
# kubernetes/swarm-system/swarm-graph.yaml).
#
# Built exactly like `swarm-allow-egress-proxy` (allow-egress-proxy.yaml), for
# the same reason: the internet rule in `allow-egress.yaml` is an ipBlock, and
# "Pod traffic is never covered by an ipBlock rule", so reaching a pod in
# swarm-system needs a pod selector naming ONE destination.
#
# WHY NO POD LABEL. Any agent pod may hold a graph ticket -- claude-code, codex
# and claude-code-browser all register the swarm-graph MCP server -- so the
# dispatcher sets no new label and every pod of the namespace is selected.
# NetworkPolicies are unions, so this adds exactly that path and removes
# nothing.
#
# WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO. It does not make swarm-graph trust the pod.
# swarm-graph answers only a ticket swarm-api minted for this tenant, this
# repository, this attempt and its generation, and it builds every object name
# from that ticket alone; this policy only decides who may knock. Until the
# service is deployed (terraform/infra/graph_service.tf, off by default) it
# selects no pod on the far side and opens nothing.
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: swarm-allow-graph-service
  namespace: swarm-tenant-u-alice
  labels:
    managed-by: swarm-terraform
    swarm-tenant: u-alice
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
    - Egress
  egress:
    # ONE peer with BOTH selectors: the swarm-graph pods in swarm-system.
    - to:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: swarm-system
          podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app.kubernetes.io/name: swarm-graph
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 8080
---
# The TypeSafe forwarder's one path out of a tenant namespace: TCP 8080 to the
# swarm-typesafe-fwd pods in swarm-system, from a pod the dispatcher labelled
# `swarm-typesafe: inject`, and nothing else (docs/design/workspace-secrets.md
# §3.5, SEC-MIGRATE-TYPESAFE; lane TS-MIGRATE-POD, part of #1347;
# kubernetes/swarm-system/swarm-typesafe-fwd.yaml).
#
# Built exactly like `swarm-allow-judge-egress`, for the same reason: the
# internet rule in `allow-egress.yaml` is an ipBlock, and "Pod traffic is never
# covered by an ipBlock rule", so reaching a pod in swarm-system needs a pod
# selector naming ONE destination. The forwarder's Service is headless on 8080,
# so a pod dials the forwarder's pod and its 8080 directly.
#
# WHY A LABEL. `swarm-typesafe: inject` is set by the dispatcher
# (scheduler.dispatch `typesafe_forwarder_on`) on a GKE live-browser pod whose
# workspace chose the TypeSafe judgment backend, only while
# typesafe_forwarder.enabled and its tenant is in typesafe_forwarder.tenants --
# never by a caller (invariant 10). A pod without it has no route to the
# forwarder; its DNS and direct internet still come from the existing policy.
# NetworkPolicies are unions, so this adds exactly that path and removes
# nothing.
#
# THE OTHER SIDE. `swarm-typesafe-fwd-ingress` admits the same label from a
# namespace labelled `app.kubernetes.io/part-of: swarm` with a `swarm-tenant`
# label (every tenant namespace, namespaces/tenant-namespace.yaml), on 8080.
# tests/unit/scripts/test_typesafe_fwd_netpol.py holds the two equal.
#
# Before the release that renders this, the owner re-applies
# `kubernetes/apply.sh --policies`: the workspace deployer's scope policy must
# name it, or every `u-*` onboarding is refused.
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: swarm-allow-typesafe-fwd
  namespace: swarm-tenant-u-alice
  labels:
    managed-by: swarm-terraform
    swarm-tenant: u-alice
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      swarm-typesafe: "inject"
  policyTypes:
    - Egress
  egress:
    # ONE peer with BOTH selectors: the forwarder pods in swarm-system.
    - to:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: swarm-system
          podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app.kubernetes.io/name: swarm-typesafe-fwd
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 8080
